suggest.autoWhat: While this is on, ohmail gets a suggestion for new senders as their mail arrives, and shows what it thinks and why — at most {count, plural, one {one sender} other {# senders}} at a time. The advice reaches every device you are signed in on within seconds. Senders already waiting are covered in batches of the same size when you open the Screener.

suggest.actTitle: Act on confident suggestions for me
suggest.actDescription: When a suggestion about a waiting sender is at least 90% sure that it is spam or one to screen out, ohmail files that sender to Spam or Screened and writes the rule for you. It never lets a sender in: a suggestion for the Ohbox, News or Receipts waits for you. Each such rule is marked as ohmail's and you can undo it in Settings → Rules. Senders you have written to, and sensitive mail, are never filed this way. If that suggestion is about a message whose sender was not confirmed — by your mail provider, or by the signature the sender's own domain put on the message — or rests only on the same subject from other first-time senders, ohmail files only that message, writes no rule, and lists it under Filed automatically, where you can put it back. Off by default.
suggest.actDescriptionUnmarked: When a suggestion about a waiting sender is at least 90% sure that it is spam or one to screen out, ohmail files that sender to Spam or Screened and writes the rule for you. It never lets a sender in: a suggestion for the Ohbox, News or Receipts waits for you. Each such rule is listed in Settings → Rules, where you can undo it. Senders you have written to, and sensitive mail, are never filed this way. If that suggestion is about a message whose sender was not confirmed — by your mail provider, or by the signature the sender's own domain put on the message — or rests only on the same subject from other first-time senders, ohmail files only that message, writes no rule, and lists it under Filed automatically, where you can put it back. Off by default.

screening.unsubDomain: {place}. {senders, plural, one {1 sender} other {# senders}} at {domain} are still waiting, so this makes a rule for the whole domain — and ohmail will also send each of them a one-click unsubscribe request on your behalf, and ask again for later mail that offers one.
screening.unsubSenderMaybe: {place}. {sender} is still waiting, so this makes a rule — and where they offer one-click unsubscribe, ohmail also asks to unsubscribe you on your behalf, now and for their later mail.
screening.unsubDomainMaybe: {place}. {senders, plural, one {1 sender} other {# senders}} at {domain} are still waiting, so this makes a rule for the whole domain — and where they offer one-click unsubscribe, ohmail also asks to unsubscribe you on your behalf, now and for their later mail.
screening.unsubFine: One request per list, once, and there is no undo for a request that has been sent.
screening.unsubFineMore: It goes from our servers, never from your browser, so your address and reading times stay out of their logs. Senders with no unsubscribe link are filed and nothing is sent for them.
screening.unsubFineMoreComputer: It goes from your computer, so the sender sees its network address. Senders with no unsubscribe link are filed and nothing is sent for them.
screening.ruleToggle: Make a rule, so future mail follows
screening.ruleToggleAria: Also make a rule for future mail
screening.footWillRule: This message moves there now, and future mail from {sender} files there too. The rest of their mail here stays where it is.
screening.footWillRuleChip: Future mail from {sender} files there too. Mail already here stays where it is.
screening.footWillRuleDomain: This message moves there now, and future mail from anyone at {domain} files there too. The rest of their mail here stays where it is.
screening.footWillRuleDomainChip: Future mail from anyone at {domain} files there too. Mail already here stays where it is.
